'Turn a face-down card in ANY arsenal face-up' needs one choice over two zones, but there is no merge-two-refs primitive, so the draft looks at both arsenals separately (LOOK_AT filter face_down scans the whole zone and stores a list; face_down:true selects is_public==false) and branches: only mine / only theirs / both. Only-branch forces the pick (SELECT_FROM_REF min 1, no STOP offered below min) per the release note that the effect is MANDATORY; the both-branch offers a CHOOSE between arsenals with no decline option, then forces the card pick inside the chosen arsenal. With no face-down card anywhere, 'picked' stays unset and FLIP_REF/DESTROY_REF no-op safely.

'If it's a defense reaction' is REF_IS_TYPE (types and subtypes both count, so 'Defense Reaction' matches the card type) wrapping BOTH the destroy and the +1{p}, since the note confirms you get the pump when you destroy. Destroy goes through canonical destroy via DESTROY_REF; the pump is MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK scoped TURN filtered ATTACK_IS_WEAPON ('your next weapon attack this turn').

Go again is deliberately NOT authored: it is an UNconditional printed keyword, so it fires from the card DB keywords field.

Known modelling gap vs CR: the real play is a single target declaration ('a face-down card in any arsenal'); here it resolves as arsenal-choice-then-card-choice (two prompts when both arsenals qualify). The outcome set is identical; only the prompt shape differs.
